newsitem.title: ECUADOR: LG Electronics sees growth in LatAm.
newsitem.headline: LG Electronics sees growth in LatAm.

text.p: South Korea's LG Electronics Inc said it expected its Latin American sales to rise 12.2 percent this year as a greater supply and broader range of the company's products become available.

"Last year, excluding Brazil, our sales reached almost $490 million. This year we expect to reach $550 million with a greater variety of products and with a strong focus on computers," said J.J. Lee, the South Korean company's president for Latin American operations.

Lee said the company's move to change its brand name to LG from Goldstar was one of the reasons for strong growth outlook. Lee was in Ecuador Monday night as part of a continental tour to introduce the LG brand name in South America.

"We want to reach a position of leadership, and we are trying to unify all products and services under one name," Lee told Reuters. "In LG, there are 62 different companies, and we are using strategies of globalization to become market leaders."
LG, the leader in Ecuador's television set market, expects sales in that country to rise to $40 million this year against $30 million last year.

"We hope to increase sales volume through domestic appliances and computers. We are also focusing more on quality and service. But I don't think the Ecuadorean market can grow 20 or 30 percent," he said.

Lee said the company was looking closely at Latin America as a possible site of new investments. LG, the third-largest electronics company in South Korea, already has production plants in Mexico and Brazil.

"We will come here as long as there is skilled labor. Five or 10 years ago, Latin America had a protectionist scheme, backing the industries of each country. They are still working from that perspective," he said.
He said the company would launch the new name in the United States early next year after its introduction in Asia, the Middle East, Russia and Latin America.
